full_judgment: 5. It appears from the record that the plaintiff filed Title Suit No.17 of 1996 for permanent injunction which was decreed in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner but on appeal the decision of the trial Court was reversed by the Court of Appeal below. The respondent instituted Title Suit No.103 of 1996 for declaration that the registered nadabinama dated 16.10.79 executed and registered by Rosmoy Dutta, predecessor, in favour of defendant No.1, regarding the suit land is illegal, forged and not binding on the respondent and also for recovery of khas possession of the suit land. It appears that an Advocate commissioner held a local inspection and submitted report before the Court being exhibited 10 and 10A wherein it was stated that the land in dispute is not the same land in dispute, although the plaintiff in Title Suit No.178 of 1996 i.e. the present  petitioner clearly stated that she has homestead in the land in dispute, which is in contradictory to the report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner. It is the specific finding of the Court of appeal below that the petitioner could not prove by submitting documentary evidence that she has possession on the suit land for which the Court of appeal below found that the petitioner is not entitled to get a decree for permanent injunction. On the other hand, the Court of appeal below also found that the land which was the subject matter of the muktipatra and claimed by petitioner as the land in dispute is not the same land because the plaintiff of Title Suit No.17 of 1996 i.e. the present petitioner failed to prove that they obtained settlement from the Zamindar by submitting dakhilas for which the said nadabipatra is not binding upon the them. The Court of appeal below found that from the perusal of the cheque/dakhilas, exhibit-2 series and the certified copy of the patta, exhibit-'Kha', that although in the cheque/dakhilas the name of the pattadar was found but the identification of the suit land and the patta number were not mentioned in it correctly. The certified copy of the patta, exhibit kha, as produced by the opposite party, shows that the land is number patta within the land of old 201/1 to 209/2 it could not be ascertained as to whether the dakhilas exhibited before the Court were related to the disputed land or not. The Court of appeal below also found that the same person   put the signatures of Shailendra Kumar and Nagendra Kumar in the dakhilas and the petitioner did not take any step to get the signatures proved for which the Court of appeal below found that the cheque/dakhilas of the settlement which were exhibited by way of exhibit 2 series are forged and concocted and were prepared in order to prove title in the name of the Zaminder inasmuch as in the cheque dakhilas there is no reference of patta number.
